text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- 100 Tamils living in Danish asylum centres have gone on hunger strike as a protest against the forced expulsion of five Tamils to Sri Lanka last week. All five Tamils wanted asylum in Denmark but received a final rejection in January 1995. Sources say that one of the Tamils was arrested by secret police on his arrival in Sri Lanka. By now 11 of the strikers have been sent to hospital, but some have been discharged.

--- Health authorities are worried about the marketing of a new HIV home-test recently introduced on the Danish market. The health authorities do not think that the test lives up to a similar test from the public health service which can also offer guidance to HIV-infected people. The health authorities have no right to stop marketing of the tests, but do not think that the Danes will use them to a great extent.

--- Film producer, Nordisk Film, now hopes to get 20 percent of the Scandinavian market for TV and Film Production before the year 2000 by investing millions of crowns in taking over TV and Film production companies in all Scandinavian countries.

--- Minister of justice Bjoern Westh is having second thoughts about legalising prostitution in Denmark. A proposal to abolish the present law won the support of parliament, but a final decision on the issue has now been postponed.

--- A new bill should make it easier for local authorities to integrate the residents of public housing estates. The proposal calls for better cooperation with housing associations on distributing refugees, immigrants and families with social problems to avoid a concentration of these groups in ghettoes.

--- Denmark's Confederation of Industry is carrying out a business campaign in the former Yugoslav republics of Croatia and Slovenia from September 30 to October 4. The campaign includes meetings between 15 Danish companies and a number of local businesses and media. Denmark's two largest banks, Den Dansk Bank and Unibank, will participate.
